replace.observe:
Inspect current or saved public camera images without moving the world.
Use when: you need named-point overlays or a saved same-round view, including a same-camera retention baseline with step=recovery.baseline_step. Current physical-camera RGB and calibration are already delivered automatically; use those images directly when sufficient. Calling observe does not advance or recapture the world.
Effect: read-only; step selects an immutable observation in the current round, never recaptures or rewinds the environment.
Returns: images, dimensions and actual or actual_historical_observation status; historical results name observation_step.
Does not: establish object identity, attachment or task success; historical images are not the current world.
On error: choose a saved step in the current round. With step, use physical camera views only and omit history_point_ids. For a complementary retention check, inspect the same camera both at baseline and now, then segment each with its matching step. Measurement feedback states coordinate units and limitations; null residuals are unmeasured. Images are explicitly indexed when present. All current physical camera RGB and calibration are delivered automatically before decisions. Depth stays query-based; precise pixel measurements use mark_point. Omitted views selects every physical camera; request a subset only for a specific overlay or historical comparison. Public robot facts: return measured pose, controlled-frame world axes, and measured finger/command state with explicit semantics. Each returned physical camera includes native RGB dimensions, pinhole intrinsics and a world-to-camera CV transform from this exact observation; historical requests use historical calibration. Derived point-cloud panels have no pinhole calibration. Full current camera coverage is supplied automatically. Numerical joint opening alone never proves a grasp; unavailable measurements remain null or explicitly unavailable.
replace.mark_point:
Measure up to eight visible pixels of one current RGB view as world-frame points in a single call.
Use when: one or more exact pixels — not an object identity, centre or full extent — must become world XYZ for a waypoint, clearance comparison or geometric fallback. Pass point_ids and points_uv index-aligned and of equal length, in the native top-left [x,y] coordinates of the named view, choosing pixels well inside the intended visible surface. For one pixel, pass one point_id and one points_uv entry in the same batch format.
Effect: read-only with respect to the world, but every measured pixel persists one observation-bound geometric mark under its point_id. Reusing a name already solved from another view verifies the new measurement against the stored one instead of replacing it, and a disagreement beyond 25 mm is refused as inconsistent_mark.
Returns: a call status of solved, partial or failed, plus one marks[] entry per requested pixel in request order, each repeating its own source_index. An entry carries its own status, xyz_m in metres when it solved, the distinct views that measured that name, and its depth-support evidence — measured depth, window radius, valid, supporting and rejected sample counts, and maximum support deviation — on success and on failure alike. The call returns one composite overlay: each entry names the colour_rgb it was drawn in, and image_mapping binds a panel to a source_index rather than to its position, because inline images are evicted one block at a time. Measurement feedback states coordinate units and limitations; null residuals are unmeasured.
Does not: track a pixel through robot or camera motion, segment or identify the object, infer hidden geometry, correct a click on the wrong surface, expose simulator ground truth, or prove reachability, collision clearance, contact, retention or success. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, not an object centre, and eight measured pixels are not a shape.
On error: a malformed call — unequal lengths, a repeated name, more than eight entries, or a view that cannot be marked — is refused whole and names the field, while a pixel that cannot be measured fails only its own entry and leaves the rest solved. Read that entry's error_code: aim farther inside the surface for depth_discontinuity or insufficient_depth_support, choose a different pixel for invalid_depth at the camera far plane, and resolve a disputed name from a complementary current view. A wrist camera moves with its arm, so after any motion discard old wrist pixels and query the fresh observation rather than hand-projecting the old image location.
